stem: What substance is 5-hydroxylysine converted into?
rationale: Lysine is hydroxylated to 5-hydroxylysine, which stabilizes maturing collagen fibers through modification and cross-linking.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: What substance is arginine converted into?
rationale: The reaction catalyzed by nitric oxide synthase, EC 1.14.13.39, converts one nitrogen of the guanidine group of arginine to nitric oxide (Figure 30-2).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Arginine

stem: What substance does carbon 2 require in the conversion of arginine?
rationale: Arginine is converted to ornithine, and its carbon skeleton serves as a precursor of the polyamines putrescine and spermine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Arginine

stem: What is the substrate acted upon by nitric oxide synthase?
rationale: The reaction catalyzed by nitric oxide synthase, EC 1.14.13.39, converts one nitrogen of the guanidine group of arginine to nitric oxide (Figure 30-2).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Arginine

stem: Which substance is synthesised by cysteine?
rationale: Cysteine participates in the biosynthesis of coenzyme A by reacting with pantothenate to form 4-phosphopantothenoylcysteine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Cysteine

stem: Which substance is synthesised by taurine?
rationale: Taurine can displace the coenzyme A moiety of cholyl-CoA to form the bile acid taurocholic acid.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Cysteine

stem: What substance is benzoate converted into?
rationale: Hippuric acid is an example of a glycine conjugate formed from benzoate, a food additive (Figure 30--4).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Glycine

stem: What substrate does glycine act on to form hippuric acid?
rationale: Hippuric acid is an example of a glycine conjugate formed from benzoate, a food additive (Figure 30--4).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Glycine

stem: Glycine requires which substance?
rationale: Many drugs, drug metabolites, and other compounds with carboxyl groups are conjugated with glycine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Glycine

stem: What substance is required by histidine decarboxylase for its enzymatic activity?
rationale: Histidine decarboxylase is a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme, classified as EC 4.1.1.22 (Figure 30–5).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Histidine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of allergic reactions?
rationale: Histamine is a biogenic amine that functions in allergic reactions and gastric secretion.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Histidine

stem: S-adenosylmethionine requires which substance for its synthesis?
rationale: S-adenosylmethionine is synthesized from methionine and ATP by the enzyme methionine adenosyltransferase (MAT), classified as EC 2.5.1.6.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Methionine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hepatic MAT-1 activity?
rationale: If hepatic MAT-1 and MAT-3 activity is severely decreased, hypermethioninemia can result.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Methionine

stem: Tryptophan is converted into which substance?
rationale: Fecal bacteria convert tryptophan to tryptamine, then to indole 3-acetate.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tryptophan

stem: 5-hydroxytryptophan is converted into which substance?
rationale: 5-hydroxytryptophan undergoes subsequent decarboxylation to form serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tryptophan

stem: Serotonin is converted into which substance?
rationale: N-Acetylation of serotonin forms melatonin in the pineal body.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tryptophan

stem: Serotonin is found within which structure?
rationale: N-Acetylation of serotonin forms melatonin in the pineal body.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tryptophan

stem: Tryptamine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Kidney tissue converts tryptophan to tryptamine, then to indole 3-acetate.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tryptophan

stem: DOPA decarboxylase acts on which substrate?
rationale: DOPA decarboxylase (EC 4.1.1.28), a pyridoxal phosphate-dependent enzyme, forms dopamine from dopa.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tyrosine

stem: Dopamine β-oxidase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Dopamine β-oxidase (EC 1.14.17.1) catalyzes the hydroxylation of dopamine to form norepinephrine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Tyrosine

stem: Guanidoacetate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Synthesis of creatine is completed by methylation of guanidoacetate by S-adenosylmethionine (see Figure 30--11).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Creatine & Creatinine

stem: S-adenosylmethionine acts on which substrate?
rationale: Synthesis of creatine is completed by methylation of guanidoacetate by S-adenosylmethionine (see Figure 30--11).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE > Creatine & Creatinine

stem: β-Alanine is converted into which substance?
rationale: β-Alanine is formed during the catabolism of the pyrimidine uracil. β-Aminoisobutyrate is formed during the catabolism of the pyrimidine thymine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > β-Alanine & β-Aminoisobutyrate

stem: β-Aminoisobutyrate is converted into which substance?
rationale: β-Aminoisobutyrate is formed during the catabolism of the pyrimidine thymine. Traces of β-alanine also result from the hydrolysis of β-alanyl dipeptides by the enzyme carnosinase, EC 3.4.13.20.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > β-Alanine & β-Aminoisobutyrate

stem: Methylmalonate semialdehyde is converted into which substance?
rationale: Methylmalonate semialdehyde is converted to the amphibolic intermediate succinyl-CoA by reactions 8V and 9V of Figure 29–22.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > β-Alanine & β-Aminoisobutyrate

stem: Homocarnosine is found within which structure?
rationale: Homocarnosine is present in the human brain at higher levels than carnosine. Carnosine synthetase synthesizes homocarnosine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > β-Alanyl Dipeptides

stem: Carnosine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Carnosine synthetase synthesizes homocarnosine. Serum carnosinase does not hydrolyze homocarnosine.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > β-Alanyl Dipeptides

stem: Neurotransmitter GABA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Transamination of GABA forms succinate semialdehyde.
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > γ-Aminobutyrate

stem: L-glutamate decarboxylase acts on which substrate?
rationale: GABA is formed by decarboxylation of glutamate by L-glutamate decarboxylase, EC 4.1.1.15 (Figure 30-12).
citation: chapter_30_conversion_of_amino_acids_to_specialized_products — Conversion of Amino Acids to Specialized Products > NON-α-AMINO ACIDS > γ-Aminobutyrate
